verdict.rationale: Pydantic AI documents agents that are generic in their dependency and output types (`Agent[Foobar, list[str]]`), so an IDE or type checker can flag type mismatches. It also documents Pydantic-model output types that force responses to match a schema. Together these give a coding agent typed signals to catch mistakes before runtime. The evidence does not show an explicit build-time or CI type-check workflow, typed tool signatures, or independent confirmation that coding agents benefit. Community reports of broken structured output on some providers and LLMs "tripping over Pydantic's magic" temper confidence. missing for 10: an explicit build-time/static type-checking workflow (e.g. mypy/pyright integration guidance), documented typed tool-argument validation, and independent hands-on corroboration that coding agents catch their own errors this way.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can rely on strict typing and schema validation so a coding agent catches its own mistakes at build time

citations.quote: In typing terms, agents are generic in their dependency and output types...your IDE can tell you when you have the right type
an agent which required dependencies of type Foobar and produced outputs of type list[str] would have type Agent[Foobar, list[str]]
